stem: Why is one dramatic close-up photo not enough to describe a room-wide IPM condition?
choices: A close-up from the most damaged plant can estimate room-wide incidence when the photographed symptom is clear and well focused
The image may show one affected tissue without showing incidence, severity distribution or spatial pattern across the crop
A high-resolution image can substitute for repeatable room sampling when the photographed tissue shows a distinctive symptom pattern
A close-up provides stronger distribution evidence than a location map because image detail captures the relevant spatial context
rationale: A close-up can document a sign or symptom, but representative sampling and spatial data are needed to determine how widely the condition occurs.
